input.subject: Re: Mesa Vista 7B water heater diagnostic summary and next steps
input.body:
Hi Diane,

Thanks for the summary and for getting the diagnostic over quickly. Before we lock in Thursday, I went back through the detailed diagnostic your tech wrote up, and I want the confirmed scope to match that finding rather than the quick-call bottom line.

The write-up on the 12-year-old Ruud RS75 notes corrosion on the burner assembly and the tank base, the thermocouple out, and a cracked heat exchanger — with a recommendation for full unit replacement (about $1,850 for an equal-model swap) and a note that piecemeal repair isn't advised on a unit this age. Agreed on that call, so let's go with the full replacement rather than the exchanger swap plus thermocouple.

Revised confirmation:
- Scope: full water heater replacement, equal-model Ruud RS75 (or your closest current equivalent) — not the partial exchanger/thermocouple repair.
- Please pull parts for the full unit swap today so the crew is ready.
- Please keep the Thursday morning (July 2) slot if the larger job still fits that window, and confirm the arrival time — I'd like to know if the full swap changes your timing.
- Send over the firm replacement quote so I can put it in the owner's file.

I'll be on site Thursday morning. Thanks for turning this around.

Best,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

input.subject: Mesa Vista 7B — Water Heater Update and Thursday Timing
input.body:
Hi Tanya,

Thanks for the follow-up call — I wanted to close the loop on the water heater before the plumber comes out.

When Hill Country ran the diagnostic, they found the unit is in worse shape than the original small drip suggested: it's a 12-year-old heater with corrosion on the burner and tank base, a failed thermocouple, and a cracked heat exchanger. Rather than patch individual parts on a unit that age — which they don't recommend, and which would likely just fail again — we're going to replace the whole water heater with a comparable new unit.

Timing for the week: the crew is scheduled for Thursday morning (July 2), and I'll be on site when they arrive. Hi Robert,

A quick heads-up on a maintenance item at Mesa Vista 7B. Your tenant flagged a small water-heater drip earlier this week, and Hill Country ran a diagnostic on the unit.

The finding turned out to be more than the drip. It's a 12-year-old Ruud heater, and the diagnostic documented corrosion on the burner assembly and tank base, a failed thermocouple, and a cracked heat exchanger. Hill Country recommends replacing the unit rather than repairing individual parts, and specifically advises against a piecemeal fix on a heater this age — a partial repair would likely just fail again and put us right back into the same unit.

On cost: a full replacement with a comparable unit runs about $1,850, versus roughly $310 for the partial repair that was first floated before we had the full diagnostic in hand. I want to be straight with you that this is a bigger number than the initial estimate — but it's the sound call on a 12-year-old unit, and it gets you a new heater under warranty rather than money spent nursing an old one along.

I have Hill Country scheduled for Thursday morning (July 2) so your tenant isn't left without reliable hot water. If you have any concerns about the replacement or the cost, let me know as soon as you can and we'll adjust before then; otherwise we'll proceed to keep the unit covered. I'll send the firm quote for your file once Hill Country confirms it.

Best,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management
